source_quality_scale.4: official primary UK regulator or government guidance; current duty, control, assessment, reporting or training action verified
source_quality_scale.3: official primary source with a material event, system, person, product, programme or scenario applicability caveat

quality_guards: Loss-of-control risk depends on aircraft type, loading, weather, flight phase, pilot competence and recovery training.
CFIT risk depends on terrain, approach design, weather, navigation equipment, altimeter setting, procedures and crew performance.
Wake risk depends on leader and follower aircraft, mass category, spacing, wind, runway geometry and flight phase.
SPAD risk depends on speed, braking, overlap, signalling, train protection, route conditions and human performance.
Rail-fatigue risk depends on roster design, shift timing, overtime, travel, workload, sleep opportunity, health and individual factors.
Influenza risk depends on circulating strain, season, age, comorbidity, exposure, vaccine uptake and vaccine match.
Shingles risk depends on age, immune status, previous infection, vaccination history, comorbidity and timing.
Pneumococcal risk depends on serotype, age, comorbidity, immune status, exposure and vaccination history.
Rotavirus-programme risk and suitability depend on infant age, dose timing, SCID status, product handling, exposure and clinical circumstances.
HPV risk and programme benefit depend on HPV type, age, immune status, exposure, vaccination history and screening participation.
CAA loss-of-control evidence is event-, aircraft-, pilot-, phase- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
CAA CFIT evidence is approach-, aircraft-, crew-, aerodrome-, weather- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
CAA wake-turbulence evidence is aircraft-pair-, aerodrome-, wind-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
ORR SPAD evidence is incident-, signal-, route-, train-, protection-system- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
ORR fatigue evidence is organisation-, role-, roster-, worker-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
UKHSA influenza evidence is person-, season-, strain-, programme-, exposure- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
UKHSA shingles evidence is person-, cohort-, immune-status-, vaccine-, schedule- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
UKHSA pneumococcal evidence is person-, cohort-, serotype-, risk-group-, programme- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
UKHSA rotavirus evidence is infant-, product-, schedule-, eligibility-, exposure- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
UKHSA HPV evidence is person-, HPV-type-, cohort-, immune-status-, programme- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer probability.
